description: The rule of the groups of strokes (contracts/README.md, section 12): from a history of writing to the strokes the sheet shows at the end, the pairs of them that are neighbours, their groups by place, the box of each group's points in tenths, and the groups of each stroke written and taken off. The cases but the last five are canvas's vectors/groups.json at its tag v0.1.2, each history as a sample writes it: times in whole milliseconds and no pressure.

cases.name: staircase
cases.description: The example of canvas's research into a child's writing and the AI tutor: a ladder of two posts and seven rungs, «30» beside it after a pause, «180 : 30 = 5» after another, the 5 erased, then 6, ringed.

cases.name: later
cases.description: «12 + 5 =», and 8 s later «17» right after it: what is written later next to old writing is a group of its own (R06 canvas).

cases.name: lines
cases.description: Two lines a cell apart, the second begun 1.5 s after the first, with no pause to think: a group each.

cases.name: signs
cases.description: 3/4 + 1/4 = 1 in fractions over bars, underlined; 3 s later «12 : 4 = 3» below: a group each, with their bars, dots and lines.

cases.name: words
cases.description: Two lines of joined-up words, each word a stroke, with the dot of an i put after its word: a group a line.

cases.name: tutor
cases.description: Two lines as tutor's synthetic writer draws them: digits 36 high, 26 apart, lines 80 apart, 1.5 s before a line and 120 to 249 ms between strokes.

cases.name: crossed
cases.description: A line crossed out at once, 0.4 s after it, which is of its group; another crossed out 3 s after it, which is a group of its own.

cases.name: bridge
cases.description: «12» and «34» far apart, a line under both 0.3 s on, which joins them; «56» and «78» the same, the line 4 s on, which joins neither.

cases.name: undone
cases.description: «12» erased and brought back by undo 3 s on, «3» written next to it 0.5 s after that, the sheet cleared and that undone: «12» keeps the time it was written, a group apart from «3».

cases.name: bounds
cases.description: Pairs at the rule's bounds and just past them: 2000 and 2001 ms, 50 and 50.1 units across, 50 and 50.1 down.

cases.name: rounding
cases.description: Dots in hundredths of a unit, in pairs. The rule takes a place in tenths, rounding half up: 100.05 units are 1001 tenths, so the first pair is 500 tenths apart across and the sixth 500 tenths apart down — neighbours both, which rounding half to even or cutting the fraction off would part. The second pair, 50.02 units apart, is 501 tenths, and the third comes out at the bound from just above. The fourth and the fifth are 2000 ms apart, at the bound of the pause.

cases.name: erased-alone
cases.description: A «1» and, far to its right, a «7» erased: the «7» would neighbour no stroke the sheet shows, so it is in no group.

cases.name: erased-between
cases.description: «1», a dash and «7», the dash erased: «1» and «7», 160 units apart, are two groups, and the dash, 30 units from each and written between them, would neighbour both, so it is in both.

cases.name: erased-within
cases.description: «1», «2» and «3» in a row, «2» erased: «1» and «3», 20 units apart, are one group still, and «2» neighbours both, so it is in that group, once.

cases.name: undone-write
cases.description: A «4» written in two strokes, the second taken off by an undo: a stroke an undo took off is taken off as an erased one, and it would neighbour the first, so it is in its group.

cases.name: cleared
cases.description: «5» and «8» far apart, the sheet cleared, and 10 s on «3» written where «5» was: the strokes cleared are too long before «3» to be its neighbours, so neither is in a group, though «5» lies where «3» does.
